rettui stopped. Its log is below.
The private key behind your address. Lost, your address is gone for good; whoever has a copy can pose as you and read what\'s sent to you. Keep copies somewhere private.
Save a copy of the identity in use
Keep another identity from a file
Settings, contacts, messages and the identity in use, in one file, to restore here after reinstalling or on another device (rettui restore on a computer).
rettui stops, the backup takes the place of what\'s here (which is moved aside, not deleted), and rettui starts again.
rettui didn\'t stop, so nothing was restored. Try again, or stop it from its notification first.
Plugged in with a USB-C cable or an OTG adapter. Tap one to let rettui use it and add it to the Reticulum config.
Nothing is plugged in. Plug in an RNode, and it shows here.
Android wasn\'t allowed to let rettui use it. Tap it again to be asked again.
RNodes with Bluetooth turned on (on the RNode: its Bluetooth button, or rnodeconf --bluetooth-on). The first time, Android asks to pair: type the PIN the RNode shows.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then look again.
Without the permission to find and connect to Bluetooth devices, rettui can\'t reach a Bluetooth RNode.
Looking for Bluetooth devices didn\'t work (Android said %1$d).
Its name in the Reticulum config:

Added %1$s. In the web UI\'s Reticulum section, set its frequency, bandwidth, spreading factor, coding rate and TX power to what people near you use (and what your country allows), then Restart Reticulum.

To save battery, many phones stop apps running in the background, and with rettui, Reticulum: messages only arrive while the app is open. Allowing rettui to run in the background keeps it reachable. It uses some more battery.
